name: 04-scenario-testing
description: How MoonLight checks itself: a scenario driving the running device while you watch.

steps.title: Tested the way you use it
steps.caption: Tested the way you use it. This is how MoonLight checks itself, on a real device, before every release.
A scenario is a script of steps, played against a running device over the same API this page uses. MoonLight has a whole library of them, one for everything that has to keep working.

steps.name: suite
steps.caption: This one stacks layers. Watch the preview: first it clears the device down to nothing, then paints a plasma on a single layer.
A second layer puts metaballs on top, added to the plasma at a little over half strength, so both pictures show.
A third brings fireworks through a mirror: three layers, each with its own effect, blended into one frame.
Then it changes things under the running stack: the plasma becomes a nebula, the grid grows, and then it becomes a wheel.
Finally the middle layer is switched off and the top one removed. After every step it measures what a frame costs.

steps.name: suite
steps.caption: When it is done, it puts back everything it changed, so the device is exactly as it was.

Those numbers are recorded for every change to MoonLight, so a slowdown shows up the day it is introduced. You never need to run this yourself: developers start it from MoonDeck, which a later clip shows.
